資料期間：2025 年 1 月起的行政部門新聞稿，以及 2025–26 會期的法: Data period: executive-branch press releases from January 2025, and bills, resolutions and roll calls of the 2025–26 sessions (including bills prefiled in late 2024). Executive-branch gaps: the Florida and Washington Secretary of State sites refuse research crawlers; New York's lieutenant governor has no separate newsroom; the Alabama and Washington lieutenant governors issued no releases from 2025; Florida governor releases for 2025 were recovered through the Internet Archive URL index and may be incomplete. The official sites of Kentucky, Arizona and Michigan refuse research crawlers, so governor releases (and those of the Arizona and Michigan secretaries of state) come from Internet Archive copies and are incomplete; North Carolina's secretary of state publishes PDFs only and Kentucky's has no news list, so neither is included; Arizona has no lieutenant governor. Batches 3–4 (Indiana, Georgia, Illinois, Virginia, Minnesota, Oregon, Tennessee, Louisiana, Pennsylvania, Iowa) cover governor releases only: Georgia and Illinois from the official lists; the others via the Internet Archive URL index, fetched from the official site where reachable and from the archived copy otherwise; Minnesota's archived captures are mostly list pages (72 releases), and Indiana's governor publishes on the state events system and was taken from archived copies, so coverage is low in both. Batch 5 (Ohio, Mississippi, South Carolina, South Dakota, Missouri, Wisconsin, Nevada, Kansas, New Jersey, Colorado) covers governor releases only; where URLs carry no date, only documents first archived in 2025 or later are included; the Kansas and Colorado sites are blocked or unreachable and the archive has no releases, so there are no executive-branch data. Batch 6 (the remaining 20 states) also covers governor releases only: Hawaii's site mixes all agencies and only the governor's own releases are counted; Delaware comes from the state news site filtered to the governor; Alaska has no archived releases; coverage is very low for Nebraska, New Hampshire and West Virginia.

Speech: GovInfo Congressional Record (CREC) full-text search for passages with the same keywords; speakers from GovInfo MODS metadata (role SPEAKING, with bioguide ID). Members are linked to their districts (House: state + district of their latest Congress; Senate: state) and shown alongside the district's trade exposure to China / Taiwan. Colours: Democrats blue, Republicans red.
＝法案本身針對中國或外國敵對勢力（抗中主旨）；Rc＝一般法案（隱私、公債、採購、: = the bill itself targets China or foreign adversaries (anti-China subject); Rc = a general bill (privacy, bonds, procurement, homeland security, etc.) carrying an operative China clause; Rp = incidental criticism. Vote shares count only R by default, because votes on Rc bills mainly reflect the rest of the bill. C = cooperation with China is the subject; Cp = cooperation mentioned in passing (including the standard paragraph on the five 2023 MOUs). K = competition framing: China as an economic or technological rival, used mainly to criticise federal policy. T = pro-Taiwan subject; Tp = pro-Taiwan in passing. Main indicators count R, Rc, C and T separately; direction and Taiwan share use R only.
